followups.problem: One dirty project that cannot be loaded wedges the shared 1 s tick. updateCommandCenterChanges throws 'project unavailable' (or any board.project or detector error) through Promise.all. The id is never removed from dirtyProjects, and tick() (line 1063) awaits this call before streamManager.pushUpdates() and the idle-close check, so the shared catch skips all of them.
followups.exploit_or_failure: A project id stays in the cached payload while board.project(id) returns null or throws (for example its folder was removed but it is still registered). From then on, every tick throws: the live feed stops for every project, not just that one, and classic /events pushUpdates and idle shutdown never run. changesSinceFullRebuild only clears this through a Command Center API request after the TTL. A user who stays on /classic (the cache is warmed at listen, so the detector runs anyway) is stuck until restart. Even if the 5-minute backstop rebuild runs, it does not drop the id while it is still in the snapshot.
followups.fix: Wrap the Command Center update in tick() in its own try/catch so pushUpdates and the idle logic always run. In updateCommandCenterChanges, use Promise.allSettled per id. Patch the ids that loaded, drop ids that failed or returned null from dirtyProjects, and set changesSinceFullRebuild = true so the next request rebuilds. Add a test where board.project returns null for a dirty id and classic stream updates still arrive.

followups.problem: The live roots and the detector's catch-up scan are recomputed only inside a full rebuild. Any scan error there, such as the SyntaxError on a half-written lanes.json that the new test asserts, rejects the whole rebuild. Also, a family or worktree root that becomes active after the last rebuild is not scanned until the next rebuild.
followups.exploit_or_failure: On a cold load, a partial lanes.json write during the catch-up scan turns a successfully built snapshot into a 500. With no watched change, a worktree run that starts after a rebuild sends no live events for up to snapshotMaxStaleMs (5 min), because its root is not in inputProjects and its parent's lanes slot only changes when a slot is claimed or released.
followups.fix: Catch detector errors in rebuildCommandCenterSnapshot: keep the entry and set changesSinceFullRebuild = true so the next tick retries. Re-run selectLiveFamilyRoots on a cheap cadence (for example every 30-60 s, using the family list cached from the last full build) instead of only at rebuild.

followups.problem: waitForLiveUpdate returns false whenever statValue is null. The tickets builtin and the --change-cmd mode always pass null, so they can only time out. The --builtin tickets path and the custom-command path advertised in usage and the changelog cannot produce a measurement.
followups.exploit_or_failure: `node tools/watch-live-latency.mjs URL --builtin tickets ...` waits the full --wait-ms on the first run and exits 1. Only the inbox mode (which the owner gate used) works.
followups.fix: Pass a predicate per mode: for tickets, wait for the project card's ticket counts or done pill to reflect nextStatus; for --change-cmd, accept a --expect selector/text argument. Add a test for the tickets builtin.

followups.problem: The builtin changes are not actually reversible. The inbox mode overwrites .swarm/inbox/state.json with only {needsYou:N} and 'reverts' to {needsYou:base}, which throws away every other field. The tickets revert sets doneAt to undefined, deleting an existing doneAt, and rewrites the ledger in compact formatting.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Running the harness against a real project (the documented use with --project-root) permanently drops that project's inbox items or metadata and the original doneAt timestamps on the first ticket.
followups.fix: In prepare(), snapshot the original file bytes (or the parsed object) and write back exactly those bytes in revert, even on error or timeout (try/finally). In apply(), change only the one field.

followups.problem: The 'file-watcher handle' metric counts lsof lines containing '.swarm/'. The live detector polls with stat/readdir and holds no watchers, so the metric is effectively always 0 (the 60 m soak reports 0 throughout). The 'no file-watcher growth' claim is vacuous rather than measured.
followups.exploit_or_failure: A real leak in fs handles (unclosed FileHandles or fs.watch on other paths) outside '.swarm/' paths would not show up, but the report still says flat.
followups.fix: Count all REG/DIR/KQUEUE/inotify fds for the pid (or process._getActiveHandles in-process) and label the metric 'open fs handles'. Adjust the changelog wording.

followups.problem: After a patch, machine.agents.total is recomputed as the sum of payload.projects[].agents.total, which replaces the full build's machine-wide value. Child/worktree rows (parentId) are included in the sum, and the full build may count agents differently (shared lanes, rows without a project).
followups.exploit_or_failure: After any live patch, the header 'agents live' counter can differ from what the next full rebuild reports (double-counting children, or dropping machine-level agents), and the number jumps at each rebuild.
followups.fix: Apply the delta for the changed ids (new total = old total - old row agents + new row agents) and skip rows with parentId. Or recompute with the same reducer the full board uses. Add a test with a parent/child pair.

followups.problem: The new binding requires manifestJob.resultFile === resultFile even when type === 'review', so the type check is redundant. The tests only exercise hand-written manifests; nothing checks that a manifest copied by the real runner into .swarm/runs/<id>/manifest.json has resultFile, one output and a model string equal to the record's model.
followups.exploit_or_failure: This fails closed, so there is no bypass. But if the runner's stored review manifest has no resultFile, or stores an alias model ('opus') while the record has the resolved id, every legitimate release is refused with review-run-state-mismatch.
followups.fix: Add an integration test that runs a real review manifest through the runner and feeds its review-record.json and stored manifest to releaseReviewGate. Drop or document the redundant type branch.

summary: No blockers. Auth: /api/command-center/events goes through the same header/cookie gate as the other APIs (a query token is refused on non-HTML paths), sends SECURITY headers with no-store, carries only project ids (no token), is capped at MAX_STREAMS and drops slow readers at 1 MiB, and the client keeps the 5 s poll as a fallback and pauses when hidden. Shared cache: patches are guarded by commandCenterCache === entry, rebuilds await an in-flight patch, patches skip while a rebuild is pending, and the rebuild's catch-up scan moves changes into dirtyProjects before it clears changesSinceFullRebuild, so I found no lost-change or flag-reset race, and single-flight and cold start are preserved. Merge-gate binding only adds fail-closed checks: manifest path tied to the runId directory, job id/agent/model match, exactly one output equal to the result file. Stress signal handling waits for the child with a 2 s bound. Evidence matches the claims: 60 m soak verdict flat, RSS steady growth -2.9 MB, heap +0.2 MB, interval CPU average 4.43% (baseline about 3.5%, with spikes about every 5.5 min from the deep rebuild), 1 EventSource throughout; latency medians 1002 ms desktop and 1001 ms phone with 0 full fetches during updates; URLs redacted. Most important follow-up: one project that cannot be loaded can wedge the shared tick (live feed, classic pushUpdates, idle close). Other follow-ups: harness reversibility and the tickets mode that can only time out, a vacuous watcher metric, the agents-total recompute, and live-root refresh cadence. Limits: I reviewed only the diff and the listed context files. I did not run any tests, and I could not check board.project's real null/throw behaviour or the runner's stored manifest shape.
